response.sql: WITH type_avgs AS (SELECT production_type_code, AVG(unit_price) AS avg_price FROM Products WHERE unit_price IS NOT NULL GROUP BY production_type_code), baseline AS (SELECT AVG(avg_price) AS base FROM type_avgs), kept AS (SELECT t.production_type_code, t.avg_price FROM type_avgs t CROSS JOIN baseline b WHERE t.avg_price > b.base), kept_mean AS (SELECT AVG(avg_price) AS m FROM kept), remaining AS (SELECT k.avg_price FROM kept k CROSS JOIN kept_mean km WHERE k.avg_price > km.m) SELECT AVG(r.avg_price) AS type_avg_price, AVG(r.avg_price) - b.base AS above_baseline, AVG(r.avg_price) - km.m AS above_kept_mean FROM remaining r CROSS JOIN baseline b CROSS JOIN kept_mean km WHERE b.base IS NOT NULL GROUP BY b.base, km.m;

assumptions.assumption: Products with NULL unit_price are excluded before averaging, so a type whose products all lack prices is dropped entirely and does not count toward the baseline.
If no types survive the filters (no baseline, or no type above the kept mean), the query returns zero rows rather than a row of NULLs; the request does not specify this case.
'Above' means strictly greater than, so a type exactly equal to a threshold is not kept.

alternatives.interpretation: If the baseline exists but no types remain after the second filter, return one row of NULL values instead of zero rows.
alternatives.sql: WITH type_avgs AS (SELECT production_type_code, AVG(unit_price) AS avg_price FROM Products WHERE unit_price IS NOT NULL GROUP BY production_type_code), baseline AS (SELECT AVG(avg_price) AS base FROM type_avgs), kept AS (SELECT t.production_type_code, t.avg_price FROM type_avgs t CROSS JOIN baseline b WHERE t.avg_price > b.base), kept_mean AS (SELECT AVG(avg_price) AS m FROM kept), remaining AS (SELECT k.avg_price FROM kept k CROSS JOIN kept_mean km WHERE k.avg_price > km.m) SELECT x.type_avg_price, x.above_baseline, x.above_kept_mean FROM (SELECT AVG(r.avg_price) AS type_avg_price, AVG(r.avg_price) - b.base AS above_baseline, AVG(r.avg_price) - km.m AS above_kept_mean FROM remaining r CROSS JOIN baseline b CROSS JOIN kept_mean km) x CROSS JOIN baseline b2 WHERE b2.base IS NOT NULL;
